description: Structural key syntax. A valid case gives the key's standard written form; an invalid case gives the reason it fails and the issue code the FDS Encoder reports for it.

cases.about: A walking lunge with a dumbbell in each hand: header, motion, orientation, footwork, load and sides.
The flag is part of the written form: a key without the accessory layer is S.
N is only for a key that carries the extended layer a.
A key that carries the accessory layer has the flag N.
Layers are written in the order m o k f s l x g r h p a.
The smallest key: the three required layers, each unknown.
Every default code says nothing more and is dropped, a:none included.
k:limbs is the default moving end, and is left out.
f:level is the default footwork, and is left out.
x:b, both sides together, is the default symmetry, and is left out.
h:none is the default held posture, and is left out.
p:usual is the default line of pull, and is left out.
a:none is the default accessory: it is left out, and without the a layer the flag is S.
A ? layer leaves the dimension open and is kept; a:? still sets the flag N.
A key must carry m; write m:? when the motion is unknown.
A key must carry o; write o:? when the orientation is unknown.
A key must carry l; write l:? when the load is unknown.
A key with only a motion is not a key: o and l are required too.
The header carries the major version and the revision.
Revision 1.0 is the latest this release defines.
The revision is written without leading zeros.
The major version is written without leading zeros.
A key starts with its type, = and the version.
z is not a layer of the exercise key.
A layer has a value; write ? when it is unknown.
Actions joined by + are written in sorted order.
An action written beside its own child is dropped: sh.ext beside sh.ext.oh.
A parent beside its child is dropped wherever it is written: a chin-up.
Two movements in rep order, joined by >: a squat, then a press.
One joint may move in opposite directions in different phases.
Two opposite actions never share one part.
^: the phase ends in flight, a jump squat.
An action done in the air is the next phase: a clap push-up.
~0: rolling on a foam roller, with no direction.
=0: a balance hold with no direction, one leg then the other.
%: a static stretch; the straight knee decides which muscle is stretched.
&: a dynamic stretch, a forward leg swing.
| joins a held part to moving limbs: a plank with a leg raise.
Parts joined by | are written in sorted order.
In a stretch, | joins two limbs taken in opposite directions.
A phase with several parts can't hold a ? part.
? may stand for a whole phase.
joint.? : the joint moves, direction unknown.
The motion can't be generic; write m:? when it is unknown.
- after an action: a short-range drive on purpose, a push press.
el.bend is not a joint action.
Only nk, sp, sh, wr, hip and ank circle.
A rep that ends in another orientation writes both: a get-up.
*: the exercise may be done in any orientation, on purpose.
squatting is not an orientation code.
The trunk end moves: a sit-up.
Both ends move toward each other: a V-up.
level is written only inside a sequence: a split jerk.
Points after @ are written in sorted order; a push-up lists every point that bears weight.
prone.pike implies the feet and hands; a bare floor is never written.
Feet on the floor under a standing body are implied.
The bench under a seated body is never written.
Feet on the floor are never written under a seated body.
Feet on the floor beside another support are dropped under a seated body: a bench dip.
Under a seated body only the feet go from a floor item; hands on the floor stay.
Feet on the floor are never written under a face-up body lying on a bench: a bench press.
The same on an incline bench; the back the orientation implies goes too.
Feet on the floor are never written under a face-up body lying on a ball: a ball crunch.
Feet on the floor are never written under a face-up body lying on a roller.
Feet on anything but the floor are written, seated or not.
Surfaces under different points are separate items, sorted: an inverted row.
A point the orientation implies is left out: supine implies the back.
A balance dome with its side named takes the child code; the feet standing on it are implied.
An accessory code is written only in a.
none stands alone: a weighted dip is l:plate@waist, never none beside a plate.
Each implement in the load has @ and where it is held.
A support code is never written in l.
An accessory code is never written in l.
A strength machine is only mac.
A cardio machine may be erg and its motion: erg.row.
A one-hand implement is one per working hand: two for both arms, so no count.
One kettlebell in both hands differs from the usual count, so *1 is written.
One arm at a time works one hand, so one dumbbell is the usual count.
At the chest any implement is one: a goblet squat.
A count is a whole number of at least 1.
? for the implement, held at the chest.
Implements joined by + are written in sorted order.
A scope the motion already implies is dropped: a split squat's legs.
Arms and legs with different patterns: one item per scope, sorted. A one-arm carry.
A movement that only rotates the trunk takes no x.
One side then the other and turns rep by rep are different exercises; one key carries one.
su is the usual hand when every action is el.flex, so it is dropped.
pr is the usual hand for every other motion.
One position's elements join with +, sorted.
A grip that changes within the rep is a sequence.
Stance is written only for a standing start.
The trap bar's neutral grip is never written.
A grip the implement forces is still the grip: a rope gives ne.
Width applies to hands on a support: a diamond push-up.
partial and deep contradict each other.
A key carries at most one start code.
A depth code and a start code go together, sorted.
Two range codes are written in sorted order.
Two line-of-pull codes are written in sorted order.
Straight legs at 90° and bent knees contradict each other.
A line can't be both higher and lower than usual.
A partner is an accessory: a partner-held hamstring curl.
Two accessories are written in sorted order.
spotter is not an accessory code; a person is partner.
A plate-loaded 45° leg press: the four standard layers, then three extended ones.
A key without extended layers has the flag S.
A key that carries an extended layer has the flag N.
A strength machine writes l s m after k.
Extended layers follow the standard ones in the order r c g a.
A standard layer left out reads ?, and the written form shows it.
"Machine" alone: every standard layer of a strength machine is ?.
Any cardio machine whose motion is row.
A bench is a support, not an implement.
A station form is cable, smith or landmine.
A value the form implies is dropped: a dumbbell is driven by gravity.
A drive the form does not imply is an extended layer.
A cable column implies a weight stack and a cable.
Two load interfaces join with +, sorted: an elliptical.
sideways is not a machine direction.
A machine guides a joint action or a verb and a direction, never a circle.
On a cardio machine c is the track; pivot is a constraint.
A cardio machine's motion is its cycle.
A cardio machine has no guide angle.
On a strength machine c is the constraint; tilt is a compliance code.
An accessory has no extended layers.
Only a strength machine has a guide angle.
An equipment key has no *: a layer is a value or ?.
A combination machine joins its configurations with ;, sorted: a pec deck with rear-delt arms.
A combination may join machine and station configurations.
Every configuration of a combination is a machine or a station.
The header carries the major version and the revision.
The major version is written without leading zeros.
The revision is written without leading zeros.
The long head of biceps brachii: a muscle and one of its parts.
The muscle key has no flag; a written flag is dropped.
Words are joined by single hyphens.
A code starts with a letter.
A key names one muscle and at most one part.
A muscle key names one muscle; a set is a category key.
The code is the anatomy term, latissimus-dorsi, never the gym word.
The side delt is the acromial part of the deltoid.
A set of muscles is a category, not a muscle.
The header carries the major version and the revision.
The major version is written without leading zeros.
The revision is written without leading zeros.
The adductors: a region and a compartment of it.
The category key has no flag; a written flag is dropped.
Qualifiers run from the region outward.
A union's terms are sorted: the lower back.
Each term appears once; a union of one term is that term.
A term another term already covers is dropped.
A muscle beside a category that holds it is dropped.
A muscle beside a qualified category that holds it is dropped.
A muscle beside an action category that holds it is dropped.
The entire musculature covers every muscle.
Of two terms that cover the same muscles, the one that sorts first stays.
a:kn.ext and quadriceps-femoris hold the same four muscles; a:kn.ext sorts first.
A term with the same members as another is still a valid key on its own.
Only a term already in the key covers others: three parts stay three parts.
An owner whose hip flexors reach further writes a union, never its own member list for a:hip.flex.
A category FMA doesn't name is a union of muscles and parts.
A union of one muscle: shoulders that mean the deltoid alone.
Ankle eversion has no action category.
The code is the anatomy term, buttock, never the gym word.
A key names at least one term.
thigh.lateral is not a compartment the anatomy reference names.
The header carries the major version and the revision.
The major version is written without leading zeros.
The revision is written without leading zeros.
A key starts with FXI=, FXE=, FXM= or FXMG=.
The nk joint moves, direction unknown.
The sp joint moves, direction unknown.
The sc joint moves, direction unknown.
The sh joint moves, direction unknown.
The el joint moves, direction unknown.
The fa joint moves, direction unknown.
The wr joint moves, direction unknown.
The hip joint moves, direction unknown.

Body point hands as a hold point.
Body point forearms as a hold point.
Body point elbows as a hold point.
Body point arms as a hold point.
Body point shoulders as a hold point.
Body point chest as a hold point.
Body point back as a hold point.

Body point feet as a hold point.
Body point head as a hold point.
Grip element w-m, the default, is dropped.
Grip element st-m, the default, is dropped.
Accessory partner; the extended layer sets the flag N.
Accessory handle; the extended layer sets the flag N.
Accessory handle.bar; the extended layer sets the flag N.
Accessory handle.v; the extended layer sets the flag N.
Accessory handle.rope; the extended layer sets the flag N.

Cardio machine: Stair machine, stepper or stepmill not known.
